sanskrit: tāni nāgasahasrāṇi sārohāṇāṃ ca vājinām rathānāṃ cāgnivarṇānāṃ sadhvajānāṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: Those thousands of elephants with their riders, and those horses, and the fire-colored chariots with their banners — by the thousands —

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ sahasrāṇi gadāparighayodhinām kāñcanadhvajacitrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ kāmarūpiṇām
english: and thousands of rākṣasas fighting with clubs and iron bars, adorned with golden banners, heroes who could assume any form at will —

sanskrit: nihatāni śarais tīkṣṇais taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ rāvaṇena prayuktāni rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: all these, deployed by Rāvaṇa and adorned with ornaments of refined gold, were slain by the sharp arrows of Rāma, whose deeds know no effort.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca saṃbhrāntā hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ rākṣasyaś ca samāgamya dīnāś cintāpariplutāḥ
english: Seeing and hearing this, the surviving night-wanderers were bewildered; the rākṣasī women gathered together, wretched and overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: vidhavā hataputrāś ca krośantyo hatabāndhavāḥ rākṣasyaḥ saha saṃgamya duḥkhārtāḥ paryadevayan
english: Made widows, their sons slain, weeping, their kinsmen killed — the rākṣasī women came together in affliction and lamented aloud.

sanskrit: kathaṃ śūrpaṇakhā vṛddhā karālā nirṇatodarī āsasāda vane rāmaṃ kandarpam iva rūpiṇam
english: "How did Śūrpaṇakhā, that aged, fearsome, pot-bellied hag, ever approach Rāma in the forest — Rāma who is fair as the god of love himself?

sanskrit: sukumāraṃ mahāsattvaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratam taṃ dṛṣṭvā lokavadhyā sā hīnarūpā prakāmitā
english: She, vile and ill-favored, fit to be slain by the world, saw him — that tender, mighty-souled prince devoted to the welfare of all beings — and was seized with desire.

sanskrit: kathaṃ sarvaguṇair hīnā guṇavantaṃ mahaujasaṃ sumukhaṃ durmukhī rāmaṃ kāmayām āsa rākṣasī
english: How could that rākṣasī, void of all virtues and ugly-faced, lust after Rāma — Rāma who is full of every virtue, of great brilliance, and of beautiful countenance?

sanskrit: janasyāsyālpabhāgyatvāt palinī śvetamūrdhajā akāryam apahāsyaṃ ca sarvalokavigarhitam
english: By reason of the ill-fortune of this people, that withered, white-haired creature committed an act that was wrong, ridiculous, and condemned by all the world.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ vināśāya dūṣaṇasya kharasya ca cakārāpratirūpā sā rāghavasya pradharṣaṇam
english: That unseemly one, for the destruction of the rākṣasas and of Dūṣaṇa and Khara, provoked Rāghava — and this was utterly unfit for her to do.

sanskrit: tan nimittam idaṃ vairaṃ rāvaṇena kṛtaṃ mahat vadhāya nītā sā sītā daśagrīveṇa rakṣasā
english: It was for that reason that Rāvaṇa, the ten-necked rākṣasa, kindled this great enmity; he abducted Sītā in order to bring about his own destruction.

sanskrit: na ca sītāṃ daśagrīvaḥ prāpnoti janakātmajām baddhaṃ balavatā vairam akṣayaṃ rāghaveṇa ha
english: Yet Daśagrīva will never obtain Sītā, the daughter of Janaka; the enmity he has forged with the mighty Rāghava is bound and inexhaustible.

sanskrit: vaidehīṃ prārthayānaṃ taṃ virādhaṃ prekṣya rākṣasaṃ hatam ekena rāmeṇa paryāptaṃ tannidarśanam
english: The evidence is clear: the rākṣasa Virādha, who coveted Vaidehī, was slain single-handedly by Rāma — that alone should have sufficed as a warning.

sanskrit: caturdaśasahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām nihatāni janasthāne śarair agniśikhopamaiḥ
english: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds were slain in Janasthāna by arrows that blazed like tongues of fire —

sanskrit: kharaś ca nihataḥ saṃkhye dūṣaṇas triśirās tathā śarair ādityasaṃkāśaiḥ paryāptaṃ tannidarśanam
english: and Khara was slain in battle, and Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras too, by arrows bright as the sun. That too was warning enough.

sanskrit: hato yojanabāhuś ca kabandho rudhirāśanaḥ krodhārto vinadan so 'tha paryāptaṃ tannidarśanam
english: Kabandha, the blood-drinker with arms a yojana long, roaring in his fury, was killed — that too was proof enough.

sanskrit: jaghāna balinaṃ rāmaḥ sahasranayanātmajam bālinaṃ meghasaṃkāśaṃ paryāptaṃ tannidarśanam
english: Rāma slew mighty Bālin, the son of the Thousand-Eyed One, who was dark as a cloud. That alone was evidence enough.

sanskrit: ṛśyamūke vasañ śaile dīno bhagnamanorathaḥ sugrīvaḥ sthāpito rājye paryāptaṃ tannidarśanam
english: Sugrīva, who lived in misery on Mount Ṛśyamūka with broken hopes, was installed as king — that too was sign enough.

sanskrit: dharmārthasahitaṃ vākyaṃ sarveṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ hitam yuktaṃ vibhīṣaṇenoktaṃ mohāt tasya na rocate
english: The words of Vibhīṣaṇa — right in both dharma and worldly interest, beneficial to all the rākṣasas, and well-reasoned — he did not heed, out of delusion.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ kuryād yadi sma dhanadānujaḥ śmaśānabhūtā duḥkhārtā neyaṃ laṅkā purī bhavet
english: If the younger brother of Dhanada had followed Vibhīṣaṇa's counsel, this city of Laṅkā would not now be reduced to a charnel ground of grief.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaṃ hataṃ śrutvā rāghaveṇa mahābalam priyaṃ cendrajitaṃ putraṃ rāvaṇo nāvabudhyate
english: Even hearing that mighty Kumbhakarṇa had been slain by Rāghava, and his dear son Indrajit — Rāvaṇa does not come to his senses.

sanskrit: mama putro mama bhrātā mama bhartā raṇe hataḥ ity evaṃ śrūyate śabdo rākṣasānāṃ kule kule
english: "My son is slain in battle, my brother is slain, my husband is slain" — such is the cry that is heard in every household of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: rathāś cāśvāś ca nāgāś ca hatāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ raṇe rāmeṇa śūreṇa rākṣasāś ca padātayaḥ
english: Hundreds of thousands of chariots, horses, elephants, and rākṣasa foot-soldiers have been slain in battle by the heroic Rāma.

sanskrit: rudro vā yadi vā viṣṇur mahendro vā śatakratuḥ hanti no rāmarūpeṇa yadi vā svayam antakaḥ
english: It is Rudra, or Viṣṇu, or the great Mahendra of a hundred sacrifices, or perhaps Death himself in the form of Rāma, who is destroying us.

sanskrit: hatapravīrā rāmeṇa nirāśā jīvite vayam apaśyantyo bhayasyāntam anāthā vilapāmahe
english: Our champions slain by Rāma, we have no hope of life; seeing no end to our fear, masterless, we cry out in lamentation.

sanskrit: rāmahastād daśagrīvaḥ śūro dattavaro yudhi idaṃ bhayaṃ mahāghoraṃ utpannaṃ nāvabudhyate
english: Daśagrīva, though a hero with boons granted, does not perceive this great and terrible fear that has arisen from Rāma's hand in battle.

sanskrit: na devā na ca gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ upasṛṣṭaṃ paritrātuṃ śaktā rāmeṇa saṃyuge
english: Neither gods nor gandharvas, neither piśācas nor rākṣasas are capable of rescuing one whom Rāma has set upon in battle.

sanskrit: utpātāś cāpi dṛśyante rāvaṇasya raṇe raṇe kathayiṣyanti rāmeṇa rāvaṇasya nibarhaṇam
english: And evil omens appear in battle after battle for Rāvaṇa — they will narrate the destruction of Rāvaṇa by Rāma.

sanskrit: pitāmahena prītena devadānavarākṣasaiḥ rāvaṇasyābhayaṃ dattaṃ mānuṣebhyo na yācitam
english: Pitāmaha, well pleased, granted Rāvaṇa immunity from gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas — but Rāvaṇa did not ask for freedom from humans.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ mānuṣān manye prāptaṃ niḥsaṃśayaṃ bhayam jīvitāntakaraṃ ghoraṃ rakṣasāṃ rāvaṇasya ca
english: This is the fear that I believe has come from humans — without doubt, the terrible fear that will end the lives of both the rākṣasas and Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānās tu balinā varadānena rakṣasā dīptais tapobhir vibudhāḥ pitāmaham apūjayan
english: The gods, tormented by the powerful rākṣasa with his boon, worshipped Pitāmaha with blazing austerities.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ hitārthāya mahātmā vai pitāmahaḥ uvāca devatāḥ sarvā idaṃ tuṣṭo mahad vacaḥ
english: For the welfare of the gods, the great-souled Pitāmaha, satisfied, spoke this great word to all the deities:

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti lokāṃs trīn sarve dānavarākṣasāḥ bhayena prāvṛtā nityaṃ vicariṣyanti śāśvatam
english: "From this day forth, all dānavas and rākṣasas will roam the three worlds forever enveloped in fear, for all eternity."

sanskrit: daivatais tu samāgamya sarvaiś cendrapurogamaiḥ vṛṣadhvajas tripurahā mahādevaḥ prasāditaḥ
english: Then the gods assembled together, with Indra at their head, and propitiated Mahādeva — the bearer of the bull-banner, the destroyer of Tripura.

sanskrit: prasannas tu mahādevo devān etad vaco 'bravīt utpatsyati hitārthaṃ vo nārī rakṣaḥkṣayāvahā
english: Mahādeva, well pleased, spoke this word to the gods: "A woman shall be born for your welfare — one who will bring about the destruction of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: eṣā devaiḥ prayuktā tu kṣud yathā dānavān purā bhakṣayiṣyati naḥ sītā rākṣasaghnī sarāvaṇān
english: "This Sītā, set in motion by the gods, will consume us — rākṣasas together with Rāvaṇa — as hunger once consumed the dānavas of old; she is the slayer of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: rāvaṇasyāpanītena durvinītasya durmateḥ ayaṃ niṣṭānako ghoraṃ śokena samabhiplutaḥ
english: By the arrogance of Rāvaṇa, that ill-disciplined and evil-minded one, this terrible destruction has come, and we are overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: taṃ na paśyāmahe loke yo naḥ śaraṇado bhavet rāghaveṇopasṛṣṭānāṃ kāleneva yugakṣaye
english: We see no one in the world who could be a refuge for us — attacked by Rāghava as if by Time itself at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: itīva sarvā rajanīcarastriyaḥ parasparaṃ saṃparirabhya bāhubhiḥ viṣedur ārtātibhayābhipīḍitā vinedur uccaiś ca tadā sudāruṇam
english: Thus all the women of the night-wanderers, embracing one another with their arms, sank into despair, tormented by affliction and overwhelming fear, and then cried out with a truly terrible wailing.

sanskrit: ārtānāṃ rākṣasīnāṃ tu laṅkāyāṃ vai kule kule rāvaṇaḥ karuṇaṃ śabdaṃ śuśrāva pariveditam
english: Rāvaṇa heard the pitiful sound of lamentation from the afflicted rākṣasī women in every household of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: sa tu dīrghaṃ viniśvasya muhūrtaṃ dhyānam āsthitaḥ babhūva paramakruddho rāvaṇo bhīmadarśanaḥ
english: He breathed a long sigh, remained absorbed in thought for a moment, and then Rāvaṇa, fearsome to behold, became supremely wrathful.

sanskrit: saṃdaśya daśanair oṣṭhaṃ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ rākṣasair api durdarśaḥ kālāgnir iva mūrchitaḥ
english: Biting his lip with his teeth, his eyes reddened with rage, so terrible that even rākṣasas could scarcely look upon him, he blazed like the fire at the end of time.

sanskrit: uvāca ca samīpasthān rākṣasān rākṣaseśvaraḥ bhayāvyaktakathāṃs tatra nirdahann iva cakṣuṣā
english: The lord of rākṣasas spoke to the rākṣasas standing near him — those whose speech was broken with fear — as if scorching them with his gaze.

sanskrit: mahodaraṃ mahāpārśvaṃ virūpākṣaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ śīghraṃ vadata sainyāni niryāteti mamājñayā
english: "Tell Mahodara, Mahāpārśva, and the rākṣasa Virūpākṣa: by my command, march out with the armies at once."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasās te bhayārditāḥ codayām āsur avyagrān rākṣasāṃs tān nṛpājñayā
english: Hearing those words, those rākṣasas, afflicted with fear, roused those steadfast rākṣasas by the king's command.

sanskrit: te tu sarve tathety uktvā rākṣasā ghoradarśanāḥ kṛtasvastyayanāḥ sarve rāvaṇābhimukhā yayuḥ
english: All those rākṣasas, terrible to behold, said "So be it"; having performed the rites of benediction, they all went before Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: pratipūjya yathānyāyaṃ rāvaṇaṃ te mahārathāḥ tasthuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve bhartur vijayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Those great chariot-warriors honored Rāvaṇa according to due rite and stood with joined palms, all of them desiring victory for their lord.

sanskrit: athovāca prahasyaitān rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ mahodaramahāpārśvau virūpākṣaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ
english: Then Rāvaṇa, maddened with rage, laughed and spoke to Mahodara, Mahāpārśva, and the rākṣasa Virūpākṣa:

sanskrit: adya bāṇair dhanurmuktair yugāntādityasaṃnibhaiḥ rāghavaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva neṣyāmi yamasādhanam
english: "Today with arrows loosed from my bow — arrows like the sun at the end of an age — I shall dispatch both Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: kharasya kumbhakarṇasya prahastendrajitos tathā kariṣyāmi pratīkāram adya śatruvadhād aham
english: Today I shall avenge the killing of Khara, Kumbhakarṇa, Prahasta, and Indrajit by slaying the enemy.

sanskrit: naivāntarikṣaṃ na diśo na nadyo nāpi sāgaraḥ prakāśatvaṃ gamiṣyanti madbāṇajaladāvṛtāḥ
english: Neither the sky, nor the directions, nor the rivers, nor the ocean will be able to shine, covered as they will be by the clouds of my arrows.

sanskrit: adya vānarayūthānāṃ tāni yūthāni bhāgaśaḥ dhanuḥsamudrād udbhūtair mathiṣyāmi śarormibhiḥ
english: Today I shall churn those troops of monkey-bands, troop by troop, with waves of arrows rising from the ocean of my bow.

sanskrit: vyākośapadmacakrāṇi padmakesaravarcasām adya yūthataṭākāni gajavat pramathāmy aham
english: Today, like an elephant, I shall trample those ponds of monkey-bands — their faces like open lotuses, bright as the filaments of lotuses.

sanskrit: saśarair adya vadanaiḥ saṃkhye vānarayūthapāḥ maṇḍayiṣyanti vasudhāṃ sanālair iva paṅkalaiḥ
english: Today the leaders of the monkey-bands, their faces pierced with arrows in battle, will adorn the earth like lotus-stems with stalks.

sanskrit: adya yuddhapracaṇḍānāṃ harīṇāṃ drumayodhinām muktenaikeṣuṇā yuddhe bhetsyāmi ca śataṃśatam
english: Today, releasing a single shaft in battle, I shall split hundreds upon hundreds of those fierce fighting monkeys who wield trees as weapons.

sanskrit: hato bhartā hato bhrātā yāsāṃ ca tanayā hatāḥ vadhenādya ripos tāsāṃ karmomy asrapramārjanam
english: For those women whose husbands, brothers, and sons have been slain — today, by killing the enemy, I perform the act of wiping away their tears.

sanskrit: adya madbāṇanirbhinnaiḥ prakīrṇair gatacetanaiḥ karomi vānarair yuddhe yatnāvekṣyatalāṃ mahīm
english: Today with monkeys pierced by my arrows — scattered, lifeless — I shall make the earth in battle a surface fit for careful scrutiny.

sanskrit: adya gomāyavo gṛdhrā ye ca māṃsāśino 'pare sarvāṃs tāṃs tarpayiṣyāmi śatrumāṃsaiḥ śarārditaiḥ
english: Today I shall satisfy all the jackals, vultures, and other flesh-eaters with the flesh of enemies tormented by my arrows.

sanskrit: kalpyatāṃ me rathaśīghraṃ kṣipram ānīyatāṃ dhanuḥ anuprayāntu māṃ yuddhe ye 'vaśiṣṭā niśācarāḥ
english: Let my chariot be made ready quickly; let my bow be brought at once; and let whatever night-wanderers remain follow me into battle."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā mahāpārśvo 'bravīd vacaḥ balādhyakṣān sthitāṃs tatra balaṃ saṃtvaryatām iti
english: Hearing those words, Mahāpārśva spoke: "Let those army-officers standing here muster the troops without delay."

sanskrit: balādhyakṣās tu saṃrabdhā rākṣasāṃs tān gṛhād gṛhāt codayantaḥ pariyayur laṅkāṃ laghuparākramāḥ
english: The army-officers, resolute and swift in their valor, went about Laṅkā rousing those rākṣasas from house to house.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtān niṣpetū rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ nardanto bhīmavadanā nānāpraharaṇair bhujaiḥ
english: Within a moment, rākṣasas of terrible prowess burst forth, roaring, with terrible faces, their arms bearing various weapons.

sanskrit: asibhiḥ paṭṭasaiḥ śūlair galābhir musalair halaiḥ śaktibhis tīkṣṇadhārābhir mahadbhiḥ kūṭamudgaraiḥ
english: With swords, broadblades, spears, nooses, clubs, ploughs, śaktis with keen edges, and great heavy mallets —

sanskrit: yaṣṭibhir vimalaiś cakrair niśitaiś ca paraśvadhaiḥ bhiṇḍipālaiḥ śataghnībhir anyaiś cāpi varāyudhaiḥ
english: with staves, bright discuses, sharp battle-axes, slings, śataghnīs, and other excellent weapons —

sanskrit: athānayan balādhyakṣāś catvāro rāvaṇājñayā drutaṃ sūtasamāyuktaṃ yuktāṣṭaturagaṃ ratham
english: then the four army-officers, by Rāvaṇa's command, quickly brought the chariot yoked with eight horses and fitted with a charioteer.

sanskrit: āruroha rathaṃ divyaṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā rāvaṇaḥ sattvagāmbhīryād dārayann iva medinīm
english: Rāvaṇa mounted the divine chariot blazing with its own radiance — his weight and gravity seeming to split the earth asunder.

sanskrit: rāvaṇenābhyanujñātau mahāpārśvamahodarau virūpākṣaś ca durdharṣo rathān āruruhus tadā
english: Permitted by Rāvaṇa, Mahāpārśva and Mahodara, and the irresistible Virūpākṣa, then mounted their chariots.

sanskrit: te tu hṛṣṭā vinardanto bhindanta iva medinīm nādaṃ ghoraṃ vimuñcanto niryayur jayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Elated, roaring, as if splitting the earth, releasing terrible battle cries, they marched out, eager for victory.

sanskrit: tato yuddhāya tejasvī rakṣogaṇabalair vṛtaḥ niryayāv udyatadhanuḥ kālāntakayamopamaḥ
english: Then the splendid Rāvaṇa, surrounded by the forces of his rākṣasa host, marched out for battle, bow upraised, like Yama the ender of time.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajavanāśvena rathena sa mahārathaḥ dvāreṇa niryayau tena yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Then that great chariot-warrior rode out through the gate by which Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa stood, his chariot drawn by swift horses.

sanskrit: tato naṣṭaprabhaḥ sūryo diśaś ca timirāvṛtāḥ dvijāś ca nedur ghorāś ca saṃcacāla ca medinī
english: Then the sun lost its luster, the directions were shrouded in darkness, birds cried out ominously, and the earth trembled.

sanskrit: vavarṣa rudhiraṃ devaś caskhaluś ca turaṃgamāḥ dhvajāgre nyapatad gṛdhro vineduś cāśivaṃ śivāḥ
english: The sky rained blood; the horses stumbled; a vulture alighted on the top of the banner; and jackals howled inauspiciously.

sanskrit: nayanaṃ cāsphurad vāmaṃ savyo bāhur akampata vivarṇavadanaś cāsīt kiṃ cid abhraśyata svaraḥ
english: His left eye twitched, his right arm trembled, his face grew pale, and his voice faltered somewhat.

sanskrit: tato niṣpatato yuddhe daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ raṇe nidhanaśaṃsīni rūpāṇy etāni jajñire
english: Such were the portents that arose, presaging death in battle, as Daśagrīva the rākṣasa set forth into the fight.

sanskrit: antarikṣāt papātolkā nirghātasamanisvanā vinedur aśivaṃ gṛdhrā vāyasair anunāditāḥ
english: A meteor fell from the sky with a sound like thunder; vultures cried out inauspiciously, echoed by crows.

sanskrit: etān acintayan ghorān utpātān samupasthitān niryayau rāvaṇo mohād vadhārthī kālacoditaḥ
english: Heeding not these terrible omens that had arisen, Rāvaṇa marched out in his delusion, goaded by Time, seeking his own death.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu rathaghoṣeṇa rākṣasānāṃ mahātmanām vānarāṇām api camūr yuddhāyaivābhyavartata
english: At the thunderous chariot-roar of those great-souled rākṣasas, the army of the monkeys also advanced for battle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ babhūva kapirakṣasām anyonyam āhvayānānāṃ kruddhānāṃ jayam icchatām
english: A very tumultuous battle ensued between those monkeys and rākṣasas, each challenging the other, enraged, each desiring victory.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho daśagrīvaḥ śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ vānarāṇām anīkeṣu cakāra kadanaṃ mahat
english: Then Daśagrīva, enraged, wrought great carnage in the ranks of the monkeys with arrows adorned with gold.

sanskrit: nikṛttaśirasaḥ ke cid rāvaṇena valīmukhāḥ nirucchvāsā hatāḥ ke cit ke cit pārśveṣu dāritāḥ ke cid vibhinnaśirasaḥ ke cic cakṣurvivarjitāḥ
english: Some monkeys had their heads severed by Rāvaṇa; some were slain and lay breathless; some were ripped open in their flanks; some had their skulls split; some were robbed of their eyes.

sanskrit: daśānanaḥ krodhavivṛttanetro yato yato 'bhyeti rathena saṃkhye tatas tatas tasya śarapravegaṃ soḍhuṃ na śekur hariyūthapāḥ te
english: Daśānana, his eyes rolling with fury — wherever he advanced with his chariot in the fray, from that direction the leaders of the monkey-bands could not endure the velocity of his arrows.

sanskrit: tathā taiḥ kṛttagātrais tu daśagrīveṇa mārgaṇaiḥ babhūva vasudhā tatra prakīrṇā haribhir vṛtā
english: Thus, with the monkeys whose bodies were cut down by Daśagrīva's shafts, the earth there became strewn and covered with monkeys.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasyāprasahyaṃ taṃ śarasaṃpātam ekataḥ na śekuḥ sahituṃ dīptaṃ pataṃgā iva pāvakam
english: That unendurable, blazing shower of Rāvaṇa's arrows from one side — they could not withstand it, as moths cannot endure a blazing fire.

sanskrit: te 'rditā niśitair bāṇaiḥ krośanto vipradudruvuḥ pāvakārciḥsamāviṣṭā dahyamānā yathā gajāḥ
english: Tormented by his sharp arrows, crying out, they fled in all directions — like elephants enveloped in tongues of flame, being burned.

sanskrit: plavaṃgānām anīkāni mahābhrāṇīva mārutaḥ sa yayau samare tasmin vidhaman rāvaṇaḥ śaraiḥ
english: Rāvaṇa moved through that battle scattering the armies of the leaping monkeys with his arrows, as the wind scatters great storm-clouds.

sanskrit: kadanaṃ tarasā kṛtvā rākṣasendro vanaukasām āsasāda tato yuddhe rāghavaṃ tvaritas tadā
english: Having wrought swift carnage upon the forest-dwellers, the lord of rākṣasas then swiftly encountered Rāghava in battle.

sanskrit: sugrīvas tān kapīn dṛṣṭvā bhagnān vidravato raṇe gulme suṣeṇaṃ nikṣipya cakre yuddhe drutaṃ manaḥ
english: Sugrīva, seeing those monkeys broken and fleeing from the battle, assigned Suṣeṇa to command a division and swiftly turned his mind to the fight.

sanskrit: ātmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ vīraṃ sa taṃ nikṣipya vānaram sugrīvo 'bhimukhaḥ śatruṃ pratasthe pādapāyudhaḥ
english: Having placed that monkey hero who was his equal in valor in charge, Sugrīva advanced to face the enemy, armed with a tree.

sanskrit: pārśvataḥ pṛṣṭhataś cāsya sarve yūthādhipāḥ svayam anujahrur mahāśailān vividhāṃś ca mahādrumān
english: On both sides and behind him, all the leaders of the monkey-bands personally carried great boulders and various mighty trees.

sanskrit: sa nadan yudhi sugrīvaḥ svareṇa mahatā mahān pātayan vividhāṃś cānyāñ jaghānottamarākṣasān
english: Great Sugrīva, roaring in battle with his mighty voice, felling various others, slew eminent rākṣasas.

sanskrit: mamarda ca mahākāyo rākṣasān vānareśvaraḥ yugāntasamaye vāyuḥ pravṛddhān agamān iva
english: The lord of monkeys, great of body, crushed the rākṣasas as the wind at the end of an age crushes the swollen deep-rooted trees.

sanskrit: rākṣasānām anīkeṣu śailavarṣaṃ vavarṣa ha aśmavarṣaṃ yathā meghaḥ pakṣisaṃgheṣu kānane
english: He rained a downpour of mountains upon the rākṣasa armies, as a cloud rains a shower of stones upon flocks of birds in a forest.

sanskrit: kapirājavimuktais taiḥ śailavarṣais tu rākṣasāḥ vikīrṇaśirasaḥ petur nikṛttā iva parvatāḥ
english: Struck by those mountain-showers hurled by the king of monkeys, the rākṣasas fell with their heads scattered, like mountains with their peaks cut off.

sanskrit: atha saṃkṣīyamāṇeṣu rākṣaseṣu samantataḥ sugrīveṇa prabhagneṣu patatsu vinadatsu ca
english: Then, as the rākṣasas were being annihilated on all sides, broken by Sugrīva, falling and crying out —

sanskrit: virūpākṣaḥ svakaṃ nāma dhanvī viśrāvya rākṣasaḥ rathād āplutya durdharṣo gajaskandham upāruhat
english: the rākṣasa Virūpākṣa, a bowman, proclaiming his own name, leaped from his chariot and, irresistible, mounted the shoulder of an elephant.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dviradam āruhya virūpākṣo mahārathaḥ vinadan bhīmanirhrālaṃ vānarān abhyadhāvata
english: Mounting that two-tusked elephant, Virūpākṣa the great chariot-warrior, roaring with a terrible thunder, charged at the monkeys.

sanskrit: sugrīve sa śarān ghorān visasarja camūmukhe sthāpayām āsā codvignān rākṣasān saṃpraharṣayan
english: He discharged terrible arrows at Sugrīva at the head of the army; he steadied the agitated rākṣasas and filled them with excitement.

sanskrit: so 'tividdhaḥ śitair bāṇaiḥ kapīndras tena rakṣasā cukrodha ca mahākrodho vadhe cāsya mano dadhe
english: The lord of monkeys, pierced through by those sharp arrows of that rākṣasa, blazed with great fury and set his mind upon killing him.

sanskrit: tataḥ pādapam uddhṛtya śūraḥ saṃpradhane hariḥ abhipatya jaghānāsya pramukhe taṃ mahāgajam
english: Then the heroic monkey, uprooting a tree, charged and struck that great elephant full in its face.

sanskrit: sa tu prahārābhihataḥ sugrīveṇa mahāgajaḥ apāsarpad dhanurmātraṃ niṣasāda nanāda ca
english: That great elephant, struck by the blow of Sugrīva, reeled back a bowshot's length, sank down, and bellowed.

sanskrit: gajāt tu mathitāt tūrṇam apakramya sa vīryavān rākṣaso 'bhimukhaḥ śatruṃ pratyudgamya tataḥ kapim
english: Quickly dismounting from the stricken elephant, that valiant rākṣasa turned to face the enemy and advanced toward the monkey.

sanskrit: ārṣabhaṃ carmakhaḍgaṃ ca pragṛhya laghuvikramaḥ bhartsayann iva sugrīvam āsasāda vyavasthitam
english: Seizing a bull-hide shield and sword, swift in his valor, he advanced upon Sugrīva who stood firm, as if threatening him.

sanskrit: sa hi tasyābhisaṃkruddhaḥ pragṛhya mahatīṃ śilām virūpākṣāya cikṣepa sugrīvo jaladopamām
english: Then Sugrīva, enraged at him, seizing an enormous boulder like a thundercloud, hurled it at Virūpākṣa.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ śilām āpatantīṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ apakramya suvikrāntaḥ khaḍgena prāharat tadā
english: That foremost of rākṣasas, seeing the boulder flying toward him, stepped aside with great agility and then struck with his sword.

sanskrit: tena khaḍgena saṃkruddhaḥ sugrīvasya camūmukhe kavacaṃ pātayām āsa sa khaḍgābhihato 'patat
english: With that sword, enraged, he knocked away Sugrīva's armor at the head of the army; struck by the sword, it fell to the ground.

sanskrit: sa samutthāya patitaḥ kapis tasya vyasarjayat talaprahāram aśaneḥ samānaṃ bhīmanisvanam
english: The monkey, fallen but rising again, delivered at him a slap of his palm equal to a thunderbolt, with a fearsome sound.

sanskrit: talaprahāraṃ tad rakṣaḥ sugrīveṇa samudyatam naipuṇyān mocayitvainaṃ muṣṭinorasy atāḍayat
english: The rākṣasa, with great skill, evading that palm-blow aimed by Sugrīva, struck him on the chest with his fist.

sanskrit: tatas tu saṃkruddhataraḥ sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ mokṣitaṃ cātmano dṛṣṭvā prahāraṃ tena rakṣasā
english: Then Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, grew even more enraged, seeing that his own blow had been evaded by that rākṣasa.

sanskrit: sa dadarśāntaraṃ tasya virūpākṣasya vānaraḥ tato nyapātayat krodhāc chaṅkhadeśe mahātalam
english: The monkey saw an opening in Virūpākṣa's guard and then, in fury, brought down his great palm on his temple.

sanskrit: mahendrāśanikalpena talenābhihataḥ kṣitau papāta rudhiraklinnaḥ śoṇitaṃ sa samudvaman
english: Struck by that palm-blow equal to Mahendra's thunderbolt, he fell to the earth soaked in blood, vomiting blood.

sanskrit: vivṛttanayanaṃ krodhāt saphenarudhirāplutam dadṛśus te virūpākṣaṃ virūpākṣataraṃ kṛtam
english: They beheld Virūpākṣa, his eyes rolled back in fury, drenched in frothy blood — made even more "virūpa" (grotesque) than his name.

sanskrit: sphurantaṃ parivarjantaṃ pārśvena rudhirokṣitam karuṇaṃ ca vinardāntaṃ dadṛśuḥ kapayo ripum
english: The monkeys beheld their foe twitching, rolling to one side, drenched in blood, crying out piteously.

sanskrit: tathā tu tau saṃyati saṃprayuktau tarasvinau vānararākṣasānām balārṇavau sasvanatuḥ sabhīmaṃ mahārṇavau dvāv iva bhinnavelau
english: Thus those two swift warriors, joined in combat, the ocean-like forces of monkeys and rākṣasas, roared terribly — like two great oceans with their shores broken asunder.

sanskrit: vināśitaṃ prekṣya virūpanetraṃ mahābalaṃ taṃ haripārthivena balaṃ samastaṃ kapirākṣasānām unmattagaṅgāpratimaṃ babhūva
english: Beholding that mighty Virūpākṣa slain by the lord of monkeys, the entire combined army of monkeys and rākṣasas became like the Gaṅgā in flood.
